title: malvastrum coccineum var. grossulariifolium

It is a shrub-like plant with showy red flowers and is native to the deserts and semi-deserts of the southwestern United States and northern Mexico. The plant has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, which include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antiseptic health benefits, making it a popular remedy for skin issues, wounds, and gastrointestinal problems. The bioactive constituents of Malvastrum coccineum var. grossulariifolium include flavonoids, saponins, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its therapeutic actions, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory properties.
